findings.reason: without a filed invocation §19 has no dispatch route at all, and the same gap was raised for §18 at the previous review and answered by filing `f-erkc-018`, so the plan's own remedy is a followup — and the live one it should replace is stale against a finished §18, which can send a coordinator back to re-run §18 rather than start §19.
findings.text: §19 carries `data-status="implementable"` and `plan-section-declarations` `s19: implementable`, but no followup dispatches it: the last filed followup is `f-erkc-018` (snapshot line 304), whose body and prompt name §18 alone, and it stays open even though §18 is declared done and its reader (`_ctest_failure_ids` at `reckon/crew/review.py:1537`, `_gate_log_format` at `:1565`, merged as `6a4142027`) has landed.

findings.reason: the two callers cannot absorb `None` as written — `promotion_gate.py:843` computes `tuple(sorted(_control_failure_ids(replay_text)))` and `promotion_checks.py:1455` computes `sorted(control_ids - reference_ids)` after `check["control_failure_ids"] = sorted(control_ids)` — so a node implementing the deliverable literally either crashes verify-gate's replay or keeps a bare `set()` for an unreadable control log, which is the silent-empty-set reading §18's rule forbids; the plan's Why names `promotion_gate.py`'s replay as served by the reader while its done-when never exercises that path, so the missing one-line contract changes what the node must implement and what it must test.
findings.text: §19's deliverable requires "`added_failures_from_gate_logs` and the promotion-side readers [to] all go through" one reader that returns "no reading for a log in neither format", and names `_control_failure_ids` as one that "reads a ctest control's failure block", yet it specifies a `None` return only for `_head_arm_log_failure_ids` and never states what `_control_failure_ids` returns for a log in neither format, nor how its two production callers handle it.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited modules (`review.py`, `promotion_checks.py`, `promotion_evidence.py`, `promotion_gate.py`), both existing test files and the cited review run all resolve; `_control_failure_ids` returns `review_module._pytest_failure_ids` at `promotion_checks.py:1277` and `_head_arm_log_failure_ids` returns `_control_failure_ids` at `promotion_evidence.py:1158`, as §19 states.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §19's done-when names falsifiable assertions (`_zero_added_against_a_red_base` false, `_head_arm_log_failure_ids` None, `_control_failure_ids` returning both ctest names) and a negative control that reddens by pointing the two promotion readers back at `_pytest_failure_ids`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate and control logs are written under the run directory, which is the same durable host path the manifest's `test_logs` and `negative_control_log` resolve to.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §19's symbols and its new test filename are mechanism-descriptive; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §19's stated root cause matches the reproduced evidence, but its deliverable leaves the return contract of `_control_failure_ids` undefined where its two production callers depend on it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §19 names one deliverable, one format-aware gate-log reader shared by the review and promotion paths, and its three write-path modules all serve that one goal.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §19 is declared implementable in `plan-section-declarations` and by `data-status="implementable"`, but no followup dispatches it.
